questions.q: Why was the Monday-morning terraform plan error confusing even though the underlying problem was simple?
options: It was thrown against the subnet NSG association, not plainly stating that the NSG itself had been deleted
Terraform refused to run at all and gave no error message
It was a syntax error in the HCL, unrelated to anything in Azure
The error claimed the subnet didn't exist, which was also false
questions.explain: The NetworkSecurityGroupNotFound error surfaced through the association resource, requiring a careful read to trace it back to the missing NSG.

questions.q: What is the very first step before running any state-modifying command in this case study?
options: Back up the current state with terraform state pull
Delete the entire resource group and start over
Immediately run terraform apply to force a fix
Disable the remote backend and switch to local state
questions.explain: A local backup gives you a known-good copy to fall back to before any state rm or import command, which can otherwise be unforgiving.

questions.q: What does terraform state rm actually do?
options: Deletes the real Azure resource and all its dependents
Permanently deletes the remote backend's state file
Removes a resource from Terraform's state bookkeeping only -- it never deletes or changes anything in the real cloud
Reverts the most recent terraform apply across the whole configuration
questions.explain: state rm edits Terraform's own tracking only, which is exactly why it's safe to use on stale entries that no longer correspond to anything real.

questions.q: In this case study, when is terraform import the correct tool instead of terraform state rm?
options: Never -- import and state rm are interchangeable in every situation
When a real resource already exists in Azure (e.g., recreated manually) but isn't tracked in state yet, so it should be adopted rather than recreated
Only when migrating from one cloud provider to another
When a resource is still fully managed by Terraform and never changed at all
questions.explain: Import is for adopting an existing, unmanaged object into state; state rm is for clearing stale entries that point at nothing.

questions.q: Why run terraform plan immediately after a terraform import?
options: terraform plan is not necessary after an import
Because import doesn't actually complete until a plan is run afterward
To automatically delete the imported resource if it doesn't match
To surface any drift between the real resource's configuration and what the Terraform code expects, so it can be reconciled deliberately
questions.explain: An import brings the resource under management, but plan is what reveals exactly how its real configuration differs from the code.
